findings: No blocking issue found in the reviewed scope. Full source and AST were read/parsed; these are static findings, not execution results.

prepare_runtime, runtime_import and verify_runtime_ready execute unchanged and must succeed before the helper sets passed. Original stable-FD environment reads, independent interpreter pin, full file inventory/digests, source loader and generated-source/native origin guards remain mandatory.

The driver calls the fixed new canonical Python with -I -S -B -X an unused private bytecode path and only LANG/LC_ALL/TMPDIR, with the original 180-second import bound. It holds verified helper bytes for the actual -c invocation.

Actual raw module origins and executable maps are recorded after the original canonical-origin verifier. Virtual Torch markers and sealed-source-name anchors remain raw observations; they are not silently treated as ordinary on-disk runtime files.

Old runtime origins are explicitly refused; the original verifier additionally resolves origins and binds each runtime byte path to the projected file map, preventing new-path symlinks from authorizing old runtime payloads.

Torch thread counts and generated-source verification are observable result fields to review after execution. The helper does not equate this preparation to model execution, typed/CHB1 admission, Hepta owner authorization, FinalUse, production or whole-job memory qualification.

The observer checks actual four-CPU quota and nice10, retains before/after physical source checks and pins, records per-command exit/timeout/raw-log hashes, and requires matching successful runtime report and elapsed time below180 seconds.
New source/audit/operation/environment-generation pins are present; independent semantic review of their generation/roster construction belongs to discovery_fix.
